derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Every field traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body per _Collab/SOURCE_AUTHORITY_PACK.md. Nothing is generalised from a client programme or a product.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: No standard specifies what a work package or job plan must contain. EN 13460:2009 Annex B 'Work order information items' is INFORMATIVE and paywalled with no public content; ISO 14224 cl. 9.6 is maintenance-record data, not package content; IEC 61968-6 is a data model. The only prescriptive list is 7 CFR 1724.53(b)(1), binding RUS borrowers only. 2.4.1 and 2.4.3 are marked judgment accordingly.

'Compatible unit' has exactly one international-standard mention - IEC 61968-6:2015 cl. 4.2.5, which names the concept, the Design and Estimation System and the Design Location. The CONTENT of a unit library has no authority at all and is the operator's.

No consensus practice exists for permit management as a process. CGA Best Practices covers 811 comprehensively and nothing else. Obtaining, tracking, expiring and closing out road-opening, railroad, environmental and traffic permits is judgment. NOTE the distinction from the CLEARANCE, which is a different instrument: a permit-to-work issued by network operations against an approved switching plan, produced by 18.4.4 and governed by 29 CFR 1910.269(m). 2.5.3 validates that it is held; it does not produce it.

AACE Recommended Practices are the only real authority for estimate classification but AACE states in RP 17R-97 cl. 1 that they are guidelines, not standards, and no AACE RP is ANSI-recognised. They are cited as consensus. Contingency and escalation VALUES are firm judgment - the RPs give method, not numbers.

NESC (ANSI/IEEE C2-2023) contains no design-review, approval or documentation requirement, and 49 CFR 192 Subpart B governs the design of pipe rather than a design process. The only federal design-records duty is 49 CFR 192.127, gas transmission only. A design-record obligation for distribution is therefore the operator's to set.
Management of change is federally mandated only for onshore gas TRANSMISSION at 49 CFR 192.13(d). DIMP has no MOC element, so for gas distribution MOC is voluntary practice under API RP 1173.
FERC 18 CFR 101 and 201 bind FPA and NGA entities. A state-regulated distribution utility is bound by what its commission adopted, which is usually these instructions but not automatically.

IEC 61968-6:2015 cl. 4.2 has no reference component for document and records management, for procurement, or for health and safety. Work packaging and prerequisite validation therefore have no natural owning component and are placed on MAI here. Note also that EN 17007 process codes DOC, SPP and HSE are NOT cl. 4.2 component codes; the two namespaces collide by spelling and must not be mixed.
